nfb23405c1ed.s: Bal Gangadhar Tilak joined the Indian National Congress in:
nfb23405c1ed.x: Tilak joined the Congress in 1890; he founded his Home Rule League on 28 April 1916.

nb3705b704d9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the order of these events?
o: The INC was founded before the partition of Bengal
The Muslim League was formed after the partition of Bengal
The Muslim League was formed before the founding of the INC
The Surat Split came after the formation of the Muslim League
nb3705b704d9.x: INC 1885, partition 1905, Muslim League 1906, Surat Split 1907, so the League came after the INC, not before.

n77d40cf4d5d.s: Which of the following was an aim of the All-India Muslim League in its early phase?
o: Launching an immediate armed revolt against British rule
Promoting loyalty to the British Empire
Opposing British rule through mass agitation
n77d40cf4d5d.x: The early League aimed at loyalty to the British Empire, protection of Muslim interests and keeping Muslims away from the Congress; armed revolt was not an aim.

nd38e00e2a8f.s: Elections under the Indian Councils Act, 1909 were:
o: Held in a single national constituency
Not held; all non-officials were nominated
nd38e00e2a8f.x: The 1909 reforms introduced indirect, multi-tier elections, not direct universal elections.

na0a476e0cbc.s: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 allowed additional members of the Central Legislative Council up to:
na0a476e0cbc.x: Additional members were raised up to 60, but an official majority was kept at the Centre.

n0efc653639b.s: Under the Lucknow Pact, a bill affecting a community could not pass if opposed by ____ of that community's members.
n0efc653639b.x: The communal veto barred a bill if three-fourths of the affected community's members opposed it.

n12b6e7ea8b3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Central Assembly bomb of 8 April 1929?
o: It protested against the Public Safety Bill
It protested against the Trade Disputes Bill
The bombs were meant to kill members of the Assembly
The bombs were thrown by Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt
n12b6e7ea8b3.x: The bombs were deliberately non-lethal, 'to make the deaf hear', aiming at arrest and a trial for propaganda.

na93b52e492b.s: In which year was Curzon Wyllie killed?
na93b52e492b.x: Curzon Wyllie was killed in 1909, after Khudiram's execution (1908) and before Al-Hilal was started (1912).

new.s: The '3 Ss' method – self-reliance, self-sacrifice and strong will – belonged to:
new.x: The 3 Ss were the Extremists' method; the 3 Ps (prayers, petitions, protests) were the Moderates'.

new.s: Which bill did Tilak oppose, showing the Extremists' comparatively orthodox stand on social reform?
new.x: Tilak opposed the Age of Consent Bill; the Extremists were comparatively orthodox on social reform.

new.s: Which pair of regional Extremist group and its leader is correctly matched?
new.x: Tilak led Maharashtra, Bipin Chandra Pal (and Aurobindo) Bengal, and Lajpat Rai Punjab.

new.s: Aurobindo set out the doctrine of passive resistance in which paper?
new.x: Aurobindo set out passive resistance in Bande Mataram; Indu Prakash carried his earlier New Lamps for Old.

new.s: Who was called the 'Father of Revolutionary Thoughts'?
new.x: Bipin Chandra Pal was called the Father of Revolutionary Thoughts.

new.s: Who is called the 'Martin Luther of India'?
new.x: Dayanand Saraswati is called the Martin Luther of India; Vivekananda was the Cyclonic Hindu and Ambedkar the Modern Manu.

new.s: Tilak revived Shivaji Jayanti as a public festival in:
new.x: Shivaji Jayanti began in 1895; public Ganesh Utsav was started earlier, in 1893.

new.s: Tilak was released from Mandalay jail in:
new.x: Tilak was released on 16 June 1914, not 1916.

new.s: In Tilak's first sedition trial of 1897, he was sentenced to:
new.x: In 1897 Tilak got 18 months; the six-year sentence at Mandalay came in 1908.

new.s: Who was the president of Tilak's Home Rule League (1916)?
new.x: Tilak's Home Rule League of 28 April 1916 had Joseph Baptista as president; Besant's League came in September 1916.

new.s: In June 1897, the Chapekar brothers killed which Plague Committee official at Poona?
new.x: The Chapekar brothers killed Rand (and Lt Ayerst) in June 1897, and Tilak was accused of conspiracy.

new.s: Bipin Chandra Pal was a member of the:
new.x: Pal belonged to the Brahmo Samaj; Lajpat Rai was the Arya Samaj leader.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Bipin Chandra Pal?
o: He was deported to Mandalay in 1907
He started the weekly New India in 1901
He lived in England from 1908 to 1911
new.x: Pal was arrested in 1907 for refusing to testify in the Bande Mataram case, not deported; Lajpat Rai was deported to Mandalay.

new.s: Lala Lajpat Rai started 'Young India' in the USA in:
new.x: Young India was started in the USA in 1916; the Indian Home Rule League of America followed in 1917.

new.s: Lala Lajpat Rai died on:
new.x: Lajpat Rai died on 17 November 1928 after the lathi-charge at Lahore during the anti-Simon protest.

new.s: In which journal did Aurobindo's 'New Lamps for Old' appear?
new.x: New Lamps for Old (1893-94) was a series of nine articles in Indu Prakash, Bombay.

new.s: Aurobindo Ghosh was the first principal of:
new.x: Aurobindo was the first principal of Bengal National College.

new.s: Who founded the Satya Shodhak Samaj (1873)?
new.x: Satya Shodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule, not Tilak.

new.s: The Bombay Chronicle (1910) was founded by:
new.x: The Bombay Chronicle was founded by Pherozeshah Mehta, not Gokhale.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Tilak's newspapers:
1. Kesari was published in Marathi.
2. Mahratta was published in English.
3. Both were started in 1881.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: Kesari (Marathi) and Mahratta (English) were both started in 1881.

new.s: At the Surat session of 1907, the Moderates were led by:
new.x: Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta led the Moderates (Naram Dal) at Surat; Tilak led the Extremists.

new.s: The Seditious Meetings Act was passed in:
new.x: The Seditious Meetings Act came in 1907; the Newspapers Act in 1908 and the Indian Press Act in 1910.

new.s: Which two leaders were deported in 1908?
o: Ashwini Kumar Dutt and K.K. Mitra
new.x: Ashwini Kumar Dutt and K.K. Mitra were deported in 1908; Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh had been deported in 1907.

new.s: Who was known as 'Andhra Tilak'?
new.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao, called Andhra Tilak, was jailed in 1908.

new.s: Which pair of repressive Act and year is correctly matched?
new.x: The Explosive Substances Act was of 1908; Seditious Meetings 1907, Newspapers Act 1908, Indian Press Act 1910.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about events of the Extremist phase:
1. The Swadeshi Movement fell in the Extremist phase.
2. The Surat Split fell in the Extremist phase.
3. The Lucknow Pact fell in the Extremist phase.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Only Swadeshi and the Surat Split fall in the Extremist phase; the Lucknow Pact came later.

new.s: After Annie Besant's arrest in June 1917, students of which Andhra college wore 'Besant lockets'?
new.x: Students of the Machilipatnam National College wore Besant lockets after her arrest on 15 June 1917.

new.s: The first session of the INC (1885) was held at:
o: Gokul Das Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay
new.x: The first INC session met at Gokul Das Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay, on 28-30 December 1885.

new.s: The Simla Deputation of 1906 was led by:
new.x: Aga Khan III organised and led the Simla Deputation; Salimullah proposed the League.

new.s: In seeking weightage, the Simla Deputation cited the Muslims' contribution to:
new.x: The Deputation demanded separate electorates and weightage, citing the Muslims' contribution to the defence of the Empire.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Simla Deputation of 1906:
1. It was led by Aga Khan III.
2. It sought special safeguards for Muslims in government services.
3. It met Lord Curzon at Simla.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Deputation met Lord Minto, not Curzon, on 1 October 1906; statements 1 and 2 are correct.

new.s: The All India Muslim League was founded at Dacca during the session of the:
new.x: The League was founded on 30 December 1906 at the session of the All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference.

new.s: The headquarters of the All India Muslim League was at:
new.x: The League was founded at Dacca, but its headquarters was at Lucknow.

new.s: What stand did the early Muslim League take on the partition of Bengal?
new.x: The early League supported the partition of Bengal.

new.s: S.P. Sinha joined the Viceroy's Executive Council in 1909 as:
new.x: S.P. Sinha was the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council, as Law Member.

new.s: Who called the Morley-Minto Reforms an incomplete deal between democracy and bureaucracy?
new.x: Ramsay MacDonald described the 1909 reforms as an incomplete deal between democracy and bureaucracy.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Councils Act, 1909:
1. An official majority was kept in the Central Legislative Council.
2. Provincial councils had a non-official majority.
3. Members could vote on the budget.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Members could discuss the budget but not vote on it; statements 1 and 2 are correct.

new.s: Lord Minto II succeeded which Viceroy in 1905?
new.x: Minto II replaced Curzon in 1905 and was Viceroy till 1910.

new.s: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms were enacted in:
new.x: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms are the Government of India Act, 1919, not 1929.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Indian Councils Act, 1892 – First indirect elections
Indian Councils Act, 1909 – Dyarchy at the Centre
new.x: Dyarchy at the Centre came with the 1935 Act; the 1909 Act introduced separate Muslim electorates.

new.s: Which Act was the longest British Act of Parliament up to its time?
new.x: The Government of India Act, 1935, passed in August 1935, was the longest British Act to that time.

new.s: Dual control was introduced by the:
new.x: Pitt's India Act, 1784 introduced dual control; the Charter Act of 1833 created the Governor-General of India.

new.s: At Lucknow in 1916 the Extremists re-entered the Congress after how many years?
new.x: The Extremists had been out since Surat 1907, so they returned after 9 years.

new.s: Who toured Kakinada, Rajahmundry and Eluru after the Lucknow session of 1916?
new.x: Annie Besant toured Andhra (Kakinada, Rajahmundry, Eluru) after the Lucknow session.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Lucknow Pact, 1916:
1. It called for the separation of the executive and the judiciary.
2. It called for elected majorities in provincial legislatures.
3. After it, the Congress and the League stopped holding separate annual sessions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The two bodies still held separate annual sessions, a limit of the Pact; statements 1 and 2 are correct.

new.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao and Bodi Narayana Rao were arrested in July 1908 for an article in:
new.x: They were arrested on 18 July 1908 for a Swarajya article, becoming the first Telugu political prisoners.

new.s: The 'Father of the Communal Electorate' held which office?
o: Law Member of the Executive Council
new.x: Lord Minto, the Father of the Communal Electorate, was Viceroy (1905-1910); Morley was Secretary of State.

new.s: Lord Minto used separate electorates for Muslims mainly to:
new.x: Minto used separate electorates to turn Muslims against the Congress; they divided the electorate on religious lines.

new.s: The second session of the Muslim League (1908) was held at:
new.x: The first annual session was at Karachi (1907) and the second at Amritsar (1908).

new.s: Who drafted the Lahore Resolution of 1940?
new.x: Sikandar Hayat Khan drafted it; Fazlul Haq moved it, Khaliquzzaman approved it and Jinnah presided.

new.s: Who became the first Prime Minister of Pakistan?
new.x: Liaquat Ali Khan was Pakistan's first Prime Minister.

new.s: The Swaraj Party was formed on:
new.x: The Swaraj Party of C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru was formed on 1 January 1923, not 1921.

new.s: At the Delhi Durbar of 12 December 1911, the capital was shifted from:
new.x: The Delhi Durbar annulled the partition of Bengal and shifted the capital from Calcutta to Delhi.

new.s: Who wrote the pamphlet 'Bhawani Mandir' (1905)?
new.x: Aurobindo wrote Bhawani Mandir (1905); Bhavani worship was a Hindu-revivalist symbol of the revolutionaries.

new.s: Vasudev Balwant Phadke turned which community into a combat force in 1879?
new.x: Phadke's Ramosi Krishak Jatha (1879) turned the Ramoshi tribes into a combat force.

new.s: The Bharat Mata Society of Ajit Singh was active in:
new.x: The Bharat Mata Society was a Punjab body of Ajit Singh with Lajpat Rai, not a Bengal one.

new.s: India House (London, 1905) was founded by:
new.x: Shyamji Krishna Varma founded India House; Savarkar, Hardayal and Dhingra worked from it.

new.s: The Ghadar Party was founded at San Francisco in 1913 by:
new.x: Lala Hardayal, with Sohan Singh Bhakna, Kartar Singh Sarabha and Bhagwan Singh, founded the Ghadar Party.

new.s: Abhinav Bharat was named after:
new.x: Abhinav Bharat (Young India Society) was named after Mazzini's Young Italy.

new.s: In June 1897, the Chapekar brothers shot:
new.x: Damodar and Balkrishna Chapekar shot Rand (and Lt Ayerst) at Poona against plague-control excesses.

new.s: The Chapekar brothers' attack at Poona (1897) was a protest against:
new.x: Their shooting of Rand was a protest against the excesses of plague-control measures.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Muzaffarpur bomb case (1908)?
o: Prafulla Chaki was hanged along with Khudiram
The bomb killed two British women
new.x: Prafulla Chaki shot himself before arrest; Khudiram alone was hanged, on 11 August 1908.

new.s: Who shot Curzon Wyllie in London in 1909?
new.x: Madan Lal Dhingra shot Curzon Wyllie on 1 July 1909; Anant Kanhere killed Jackson at Nasik.

new.s: Vanchi Aiyar's action of 1911 was linked with the Swadeshi Steam Navigation agitation of:
new.x: Vanchi Aiyar was linked to the Bharata Matha Association and V.O. Chidambaram Pillai's Swadeshi Steam Navigation agitation.

new.s: How many persons were accused in the Alipore Bomb Case?
new.x: 49 were accused, including Aurobindo and Barindra Ghosh; 19 were sentenced.

new.s: In the Alipore Bomb Case, Barindra Kumar Ghosh was sentenced to:
new.x: Barindra got life (Andaman Cellular Jail), while Aurobindo was acquitted.

new.s: The Alipore Bomb Case was triggered by a police raid on a bomb factory at:
new.x: The Maniktala bomb factory in Calcutta was raided after Muzaffarpur, leading to the Alipore case.

new.s: Who threw the bomb at Lord Hardinge in Delhi in 1912?
new.x: Basanta Kumar Biswas threw the bomb; Rash Behari Bose led the plan and escaped.

new.s: What happened to Lord Hardinge in the bomb attack of 23 December 1912?
o: He was not in the procession
new.x: Hardinge was injured, not killed, during his state entry into Delhi.

new.s: The Howrah (Howrah-Sibpur) Conspiracy Case of 1910 is associated with:
new.x: The Howrah Conspiracy Case (1910) is associated with Bagha Jatin.

new.s: Bagha Jatin died in a gunfight in 1915 at:
new.x: Bagha Jatin, leader of the Indo-German plan, died in a gunfight at Balasore in 1915.

new.s: The Defence of India Act was enacted in:
new.x: The Defence of India Act came in 1915; the 1907 deportation was under Regulation III of 1818.

new.s: Savarkar's 'Hindutva' was published in:
new.x: Hindutva appeared in 1923; The Indian War of Independence, 1857 in 1909.

new.s: In which case was V.D. Savarkar sentenced to life in the Andamans?
new.x: Savarkar got life in the Cellular Jail, Andamans, in the Nasik case.

new.s: The Chittagong Armoury Raid took place in:
new.x: The Chittagong Armoury Raid was in 1930.

new.s: Which book was written by Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee?
new.x: Jogesh Chatterjee wrote In Search of Freedom; Bandi Jiwan was by Sachindranath Sanyal.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about birth years of revolutionaries:
1. Bhagat Singh was born in 1907.
2. Chandrashekhar Azad was born in 1906.
3. Khudiram Bose was born in 1889.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All are correct: Bhagat Singh 28 Sep 1907, Azad 23 Jul 1906, Khudiram 3 Dec 1889.

new.s: In the Saunders killing of 1928, the intended target was:
new.x: The revolutionaries aimed at James A. Scott to avenge the lathi-charge on Lajpat Rai; Saunders was killed instead.

new.s: The journal 'Talwar' was associated with:
new.x: Talwar was Virendranath Chattopadhyay's; Islamic Fraternity was Barkatullah's and Swadesh Sevak G.D. Kumar's.

new.s: 'Why I am an Atheist' was written by:
new.x: Bhagat Singh wrote Why I am an Atheist; Bhagwati Charan Vohra wrote The Philosophy of the Bomb.

new.s: The revolutionary manual 'Mukti Kon Pathe' (1906) is associated with:
new.x: Mukti Kon Pathe (1906) was Barindra Kumar Ghosh's manual.

new.s: The Berlin Committee (1915) was associated with:
o: Lala Hardayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna
new.x: The Berlin Committee of Chattopadhyaya and Bhupendranath Dutta sought German and Turkish help.

new.s: The Ghadar revolt fixed for 21 February 1915 was planned in:
new.x: The Ghadar revolt was fixed for 21 February 1915 in Punjab but was betrayed.

new.s: How many passengers were aboard the Komagata Maru (1914)?
new.x: The Komagata Maru carried 376 mostly Sikh passengers; the Budge Budge firing killed 22.

new.s: The Budge Budge firing on the returning Komagata Maru passengers killed:
new.x: 22 were killed at Budge Budge when the passengers were forced back to India.

new.s: Which unit rose in the Singapore Mutiny of February 1915?
new.x: Indian troops of the 5th Light Infantry rose under Ghadar influence.

new.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju was killed on:
new.x: Raju was killed on 7 May 1924, not 1922; 22 August 1922 was his first attack, on Chintapalli.

new.s: The Rampa Rebellion of Alluri Sitarama Raju was directed against the:
new.x: Raju rose against the Muttadari system, the forest laws and Tahsildar Bastian.

new.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Kakori train action
2. Hindustan Republican Association
3. Hindustan Socialist Republican Association
4. Naujawan Bharat Sabha
new.x: HRA 1924, Kakori 1925, Naujawan Bharat Sabha 1926, HSRA 1928.
